question: Should promptly-prompt remain ineligible for plugin admission until its OpenClaw manifest claim is backed by a complete native package and the standard executable-package trust evidence?
rationale: Its only demonstrated executable path is Claude-specific, while catalog admission would represent it as an installable OpenClaw plugin and cross the package-compatibility and prompt-interception security boundary.

options.title: Require complete OpenClaw artifact
options.body: Keep this issue open until the publisher adds a real package and OpenClaw entrypoint, then supplies ownership, provenance, validation, scans, and live proof.

options.title: Use skill-only publication
options.body: Decline plugin-family admission and use the skill publication path unless the executable runtime is genuinely ported to OpenClaw.

recommendation.title: Require complete OpenClaw artifact
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until the publisher adds a real package and OpenClaw entrypoint, then supplies ownership, provenance, validation, scans, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and most heavily maintained the package-validation and security contract governing this decision.
